intervals.label: physics run
intervals.quote: In the first year of physics run, the E949 experiment at Brookhaven National Laboratory has already collected 1.8x10^12 kaons stopping in the target.
intervals.note: The source describes this as the 'first year of physics run' as of a September 2004 paper; no source fetched this session gives an explicit calendar start year (commonly cited elsewhere as 2002) or an explicit end date for data-taking, so those are left unrecorded rather than guessed.

intervals.label: completed
intervals.note: 2009-02 is the date of the final combined E787+E949 result paper, used as a lower bound for when the programme was treated as complete; no source fetched this session states an explicit end-of-data-taking date.

physics_goals.value: Search for and measure the branching ratio of the rare kaon decay K+ -> pi+ nu nubar using stopped kaons, as the successor to E787

summary.plain: E949 was a Brookhaven National Laboratory experiment that stopped kaons in a detector to catch the same ultra-rare decay NA62 studies today -- a kaon turning into a pion and two invisible neutrinos -- continuing the earlier E787 experiment.
summary.technical: Stopped-kaon experiment at Brookhaven (successor to E787) measuring K+ -> pi+ nu nubar; by its first year of physics running (per a September 2004 paper) had collected 1.8x10^12 stopped kaons, giving a combined E787+E949 branching ratio of (1.47+1.30-0.89)x10^-10; the final combined analysis (PRD 79, 092004, 2009) found seven total signal events and Br = (1.73+1.15-1.05)x10^-10.
